title: Artistic self-efficacy scale for middle school students: Development, validity, reliability, and measurement invariance evidence
text_snippet: Artistic self-efficacy scale for middle school students: Development, validity, reliability, and measurement invariance evidence This study developed an artistic self-efficacy scale for students in Grades 5–8 and examined its psychometric properties in visual arts education. A quantitative scale-development and validation design was used. Separate groups of experts and middle school students participated in content review, pilot testing, exploratory analysis, confirmatory analysis, reliability assessment, and measurement-invariance testing. Items were generated from the literature and refined through expert review and student feedback. Exploratory analyses yielded a theoretically interpretable structure involving technical application and material use, aesthetic evaluation and interpretation, and innovative production and adaptive strategies, while also indicating a strong general artistic self-efficacy component. Confirmatory analyses showed that the correlated three-factor model represented the data better than a single-factor model, and a higher-order model also supported the interpretation of an overall score. title: The mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationship between learner autonomy and early maladaptive schemas among learners of English as a foreign language
text_snippet: The mediating role of self-efficacy in the relationship between learner autonomy and early maladaptive schemas among learners of English as a foreign language The present study aimed to examine the impact of early maladaptive schemas on university students’ levels of autonomous learning and to investigate the mediating role of self-efficacy in this association. The participants were 249 undergraduate students aged 18 to 32, enrolled at a public university in Türkiye. Data were collected online using the Autonomous Learning Scale, the Young Schema Questionnaire–Short Form, and the General Self-Efficacy Scale. The data were analyzed using correlational and mediation analyses to explore both direct and indirect effects. The findings indicated that the schemas of abandonment, failure, defectiveness, submission, and dependence were negatively associated with autonomous learning. Conversely, high standards schema showed a positive relationship with autonomous learning. Self-efficacy was found to significantly mediate the relationship between these early maladaptive schemas and autonomous learning, suggesting that students’ beliefs in their abilities play a crucial role in this mechanism.

title: Examining pre-service primary school teachers’ views on fostering environmental awareness in elementary students
text_snippet: Examining pre-service primary school teachers’ views on fostering environmental awareness in elementary students Pre-service primary teachers’ perceptions are vital for fostering sustainable environmental consciousness. This qualitative case study explored the views of 20 pre-service teachers at a university in the central district of Tokat province on cultivating environmental awareness among elementary students. Participants from different year cohorts were chosen through criterion sampling. Data were collected via semi-structured, expert-validated interviews lasting 9 to 10 minutes, recorded and fully transcribed. Content analysis with independent comparative coding and peer review enhanced reliability. Ethical principles, including voluntary participation and confidentiality, were rigorously upheld. Results indicated strong support for early environmental education and highlighted interactive strategies—observation, experimentation, and project-based learning shape perceptions and behaviors. Participants stressed moving beyond theoretical coverage toward practical, student-centered experiences that influence habits. title: An innovative approach in mathematics education: A review of digital storytelling
text_snippet: An innovative approach in mathematics education: A review of digital storytelling The integration of digital technologies into educational processes necessitates the development of innovative and student-centered approaches in mathematics education. In this context, digital storytelling has emerged as a noteworthy instructional method due to its narrative-based structure, its ability to integrate multimedia elements, and its positioning of learners as active creators. This study examines the concept of digital storytelling within the context of mathematics education through a theoretical review of both national and international literature. Research concerning its implementation in mathematics teaching environments is analyzed and presented. The primary purpose of the study is to systematically evaluate the effects of digital storytelling on mathematical learning, problem-solving skills, attitudes toward mathematics, motivation, and twenty-first-century competencies. Furthermore, the study seeks to identify the contributions of digital storytelling to the concretization of mathematical concepts and their connection to real-life contexts, its areas of application within instructional processes, and the limitations encountered during implementation. title: The evaluation of students’ opinions on the use of “Kahoot!” in Turkish language education
text_snippet: The evaluation of students’ opinions on the use of “Kahoot!” in Turkish language education This study aims to examine the opinions of undergraduate students enrolled in the Turkish Language Teaching Program at Tokat Gaziosmanpaşa University regarding the use of Kahoot! in the Listening Education course. Designed within a qualitative research framework, the study employed semi-structured interviews as the primary data collection method. The implementation process involved the integration of Kahoot!-based activities into the Listening Education course over a four-week period. Following the implementation, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 students who were randomly selected from those who actively participated in the process. The data collected were analyzed using descriptive analysis techniques and were further supported by quantitative indicators in the form of frequencies. The findings indicate that the majority of participants held positive views toward the use of Kahoot!. Students reported that Kahoot! enhanced the enjoyment of the classroom environment, increased motivation and active participation, and contributed to the reinforcement and retention of learned content. title: Predictors of pre-service teachers’ attitudes toward artificial intelligence: An examination of AI literacy and anxiety
text_snippet: Predictors of pre-service teachers’ attitudes toward artificial intelligence: An examination of AI literacy and anxiety The primary purpose of this study is to investigate the relationships among pre-service teachers’ general attitudes toward artificial intelligence, their levels of AI anxiety, and their AI literacy skills. As artificial intelligence continues to transform various aspects of education, understanding the attitudes of future educators toward this technology has become increasingly important. The study group consisted of pre-service teachers studying at different universities in Türkiye, the majority of whom were female. Data collection instruments included the General Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence Scale, the AI Anxiety Scale, the AI Literacy Scale, and a Personal Information Form designed by the researchers. Data was analyzed through Pearson correlation analysis and multiple regression analysis using SPSS and AMOS software. The findings revealed that AI literacy was positively associated with pre-service teachers’ attitudes toward artificial intelligence, while AI anxiety was negatively associated with such attitudes. title: Development study of the self-soothing skills scale for adolescents
text_snippet: Development study of the self-soothing skills scale for adolescents The aim of this research is to explore the self-soothing skills of adolescents and to develop a valid and reliable measurement tool for assessing these skills. The research was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with middle school students aged 11 to 14 in order to identify the self-soothing strategies adolescents use in emotionally distressing situations. The interview data were analyzed through content analysis, and five sub-themes related to adolescents’ self-soothing skills were identified. Based on the qualitative findings, relevant literature, and expert opinions, an item pool for the Self-Soothing Skills Scale for Adolescents was created. In the quantitative phase, the draft scale was administered to middle school students to examine its psychometric properties. Exploratory factor analysis revealed a multidimensional structure, and confirmatory factor analysis supported the construct validity of the scale. title: The effect of prosocial behavior education program on preschoolers' prosociality levels and an examination of fathers' prosociality levels

The research was carried out with the participation of a total of 30 children and their fathers: 15 children in the experimental group and 15 in the control group. These participants were students (aged 50-72 months) enrolled in two different kindergartens located in the Etimesgut district of Ankara Province. Data were collected using a Demographic Form, the Child Prosociality Scale (Father and Teacher Forms), the Adult Prosociality Scale (Father Form), and two Prosocial Behavior Interview Forms (Father and Child Forms). The "Prosocial Behavior Training Activities" were implemented as 24 sessions over eight weeks with the experimental group. The control group continued standard educational activities without intervention until the conclusion of data collection. Data was analyzed using the SPSS statistical software package. title: Sustainable development goals in the English language curriculum of science and art centers in Türkiye
text_snippet: Sustainable development goals in the English language curriculum of science and art centers in Türkiye The purpose of this study is to examine the English Language Curriculum of Science and Art Centers (SAC) in line with the Sustainable Development Goals. These goals are defined as Quality Education, Gender Equality, Reduced Inequalities, and Partnerships for the Goals. The research was designed according to a qualitative design and was conducted using the document analysis method. The data source is the SAC English Language Curriculum published by the Ministry of National Education in 2024. According to the findings, the outcomes that align with the Quality Education goal support students' student-centered learning, productivity, communication, and critical thinking skills. However, the limited coverage of the Gender Equality and Reduced Inequalities goals in terms of content and representation creates a gap in the program's inclusiveness. The Partnerships for Goals objective is more prevalent in higher-level modules and is not evenly distributed throughout the program. Based on these findings, it is recommended that the SAC English language curriculum be integrated into the Sustainable Development Goals in a more systematic and holistic manner. title: Creative thinking in education: A comprehensive review on theory, instruction, and assessment
text_snippet: Creative thinking in education: A comprehensive review on theory, instruction, and assessment Creative thinking has long been the subject of growing interest in many fields as a multidimensional skill that refers to individuals' capacity to generate original, flexible, and functional ideas. Recognized as a skill that must be acquired through education, creative thinking is also one of the life skills of the 21st century. Based on the knowledge that every individual has creative potential, educational environments that support creative thinking, creative teachers, and the educational measurement of creative thinking form the framework of this study. The aim of this review study is to examine the theoretical foundations of creative thinking, measurement approaches, and their reflections in educational environments within a holistic framework. The study comprehensively examines the definitions and theoretical models of creative thinking, the tools used to measure creative thinking skills, and the characteristics of learning environments that support creative thinking. The study reveals that creative thinking is not limited to individual potential but is shaped by the pedagogical environment and assessment culture, offering practical insights for teachers and researchers.

title: EFL learners’ preferences for written corrective feedback: Does personality matter?
text_snippet: EFL learners’ preferences for written corrective feedback: Does personality matter? The surge in popularity of written corrective feedback (WCF) within ESL and EFL settings has been notable in recent years. However, a neglected facet of this common practice pertains to the antecedents of students’ opinions and preferences regarding this widespread instructional strategy due to the ongoing debates concerning its long-term effectiveness. This study employed quantitative methodology to investigate the WCF preferences and personality traits of EFL learners and addressed a research gap by examining the potential relationship between these two variables since limited research delved into the role that learner-related factors play in shaping students’ WCF preferences. Participants included 371 English-major students at a Turkish state university. Findings revealed a preference for unfocused, teacher-initiated, metalinguistic feedback with specific and detailed comments on content and organization, marked in red ink. title: Building AI self-efficacy in EFL teachers: A mixed-methods study of professional development using an artificial intelligence-based lesson planning tool
text_snippet: Building AI self-efficacy in EFL teachers: A mixed-methods study of professional development using an artificial intelligence-based lesson planning tool This explanatory mixed-method sequential study examined the artificial intelligence (AI) self-efficacy in English as a foreign language (EFL) teachers using an intervention-based, two-week program centered around Diffit, an AI-driven, lesson planning and instructional differentiation tool. 35 in-service EFL teachers (80% female, M age = 38.7 years, teaching experience 2-25 years) were enrolled in the study. The AI Self-efficacy Scale (AISES) was used to gather quantitative data in a one-group pretest-posttest study, and the qualitative data were in the form of written reflections of teachers using inductive thematic coding. The results of the Wilcoxon signed-rank test showed that the outcome of AI self-efficacy between pretest and posttest was statistically different. The qualitative analysis revealed seven major themes that explained this enhancement: AI self-efficacy, efficiency and time-saving, differentiation and access, quality control and teacher judgment, barriers to implementation, student engagement, and ethics and data concerns. title: Increasing cooperation during medical examination in children with autism spectrum disorder
text_snippet: Increasing cooperation during medical examination in children with autism spectrum disorder This study aims to examine the effects of a shaping strategy on increasing children with autism spectrum disorder's cooperation during general medical examinations and the generalizability of the acquired adaptation to natural medical environments. The study also examined the parents' opinions of the participating children about the study. The participants of this study, which was conducted with a changing criterion design, were three boys aged 3-6 years diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder. Research findings show that the teaching package, which included a shaping strategy, improved participants' cooperation with the general medical examination. It was observed that the participants demonstrated the cooperation they had achieved during medical examinations in natural medical environments. The study’s social validity findings also showed that the intervention provided significant improvements for participants and their parents.

title: Conceptual misconceptions regarding DNA and the genetic code in 8th-grade students' understanding of genetic information
text_snippet: Conceptual misconceptions regarding DNA and the genetic code in 8th-grade students' understanding of genetic information The purpose of this study is to identify misconceptions among eighth-grade students regarding the "DNA and Genetic Code" unit through a word association test. The study group consisted of 186 students, 102 girls and 84 boys, attending a public middle school in Bitlis province during the 2024-2025 academic year. The convenience sampling method, one of the purposeful sampling types, was used in selecting the research group. The study group was selected randomly without any distinction between students and classes. The phenomenological design was used as the research design in the study. The word association test was used as the data collection tool. Inductive content analysis was used in the analysis of the data. The results of the research revealed that students had misconceptions about DNA and genetic code units, perceived the unit concepts abstractly, and that the vast majority of students confused basic concepts (e.g., genotype and phenotype, DNA and chromosome). title: What qualities should a multicultural teacher have?
text_snippet: What qualities should a multicultural teacher have? The current study aims to identify the characteristics that a multicultural teacher should possess based on the perspectives of in-service and pre-service teachers. The study was conducted within the framework of a basic qualitative research design involving in-service and pre-service teachers as participants. Data were collected through an open-ended questionnaire and were analyzed by using content analysis. The findings indicate that both groups expressed largely similar views regarding multicultural teacher characteristics in terms of values, skills, competencies, and conceptual biases. However, the in-service teachers placed greater emphasis on personal development compared to the pre-service teachers. Among the identified dimensions, values emerged as the most frequently emphasized theme, while empathy and communication skills were highlighted as essential skills for multicultural teaching. The in-service teachers emphasized technology use as an important professional competency, whereas the pre-service teachers focused more on cultural knowledge and inclusivity. title: Research trends on sustainability in higher education
text_snippet: Research trends on sustainability in higher education This study examined prevailing themes and emerging areas of interest in sustainability research in higher education. This study used a bibliometric review of articles indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database from first mention through the end of 2024. The results showed that there is a growing acceleration in both publication and citation numbers, and that the majority of published studies. title: A comparative analysis of the 2018 and 2024 religious culture and ethics curricula (grades 9–12) within the Türkiye century education model
text_snippet: A comparative analysis of the 2018 and 2024 religious culture and ethics curricula (grades 9–12) within the Türkiye century education model The objectives and content of religious education in schools are determined by curriculum frameworks. The purpose of this study is to identify the similarities and differences between the 2018 Religious Culture and Ethics Course (Grades 9–12) curriculum and the 2024 curriculum developed within the framework of the Türkiye Century Education Model. This study is based on the analysis of the 2018 and 2024 Religious Culture and Ethics curricula. Employing qualitative research methods, the study utilizes document analysis as its primary data collection technique. Both curricula were examined in terms of their educational philosophies, fundamental approaches, vision, teaching principles, instructional methods and techniques, assessment and evaluation strategies, the role of teachers, the teaching of values and concepts, learning environments, instructional resources, and unit structures. Both curricula adopt a student-centered approach to religious and moral education. title: Science achievement from grades 4 to 8: Structural equation modeling using longitudinal data
text_snippet: Science achievement from grades 4 to 8: Structural equation modeling using longitudinal data This study investigates the longitudinal development of students’ academic achievement and the predictive role of science scores in grades 4–8 on High School Entrance Exam outcomes in Türkiye. The data were examined through the application of two separate structural equation models. The constructed models assess the temporal, autoregressive relationships among academic performance from 4th to 8th grade and examine the direct and indirect effects on the High School Entrance Exam performance using longitudinal data. According to the results, science achievement at each grade level significantly predicts academic performance in subsequent years and shows both direct and indirect effects on High School Entrance Exam scores. Although gender showed a small but statistically significant effect at certain grade levels, it did not have a meaningful or practically significant impact on High School Entrance Exam science achievement. Both models demonstrated good fit and explained more than 50% of the variance in High School Entrance Exam science scores. When the two models were compared, Grade 6 science achievement demonstrated a stronger predictive effect on High School Entrance Exam scores.

title: Turkish adaptation and psychometric validation of a short version of the pragmatic and hedonic quality scale
text_snippet: Turkish adaptation and psychometric validation of a short version of the pragmatic and hedonic quality scale The purpose of this study was to confirm the validity and reliability of the Turkish version of the Pragmatic and Hedonic Quality Scale and to examine its psychometric properties. To achieve this, linguistic equivalence, confirmatory factor analysis, and validity and reliability analyses were conducted on two independent samples (N₁= 264, N₂ = 469). The results confirmed that the adapted scale retained its three-factor structure, consistent with the original version, with corresponding items forming the same sub-dimensions. The model demonstrated an acceptable fit to the data. The CFA results indicated that the model fit was within the recommended thresholds in both samples. Reliability analyses indicated that the internal consistency coefficients for the three factors and the whole scale ranged from .71 to .93, and the overall scale showed high reliability. The findings of this study confirm that the Turkish version of the scale preserves the original three-factor structure and demonstrates strong construct validity and reliability.

title: Can augmented reality-based stories reduce English speaking anxiety? An experimental study
text_snippet: Can augmented reality-based stories reduce English speaking anxiety? An experimental study Augmented reality (AR) is a technology that enables the simultaneous integration of the real and virtual worlds in the same space by overlaying computer-generated digital elements onto objects in the physical world, offering rich interactive experiences. The aim of this study is to investigate the impact of AR-supported storytelling on students’ anxiety about speaking English. The study employed a quasi-experimental design, a type of experimental design. The participants consisted of 47 fifth-grade students. Twenty-three participants were in the experimental group, while 24 were in the control group. The intervention was conducted over a four-week period, totaling 12 class hours at a rate of three class hours per week. While AR-supported storytelling was implemented via mobile devices in the experimental group, the same stories were covered in a traditional manner using printed materials in the control group. title: Perceptions of artificial intelligence among gifted primary school students: An analysis from cognitive, emotional, and social perspectives
text_snippet: Perceptions of artificial intelligence among gifted primary school students: An analysis from cognitive, emotional, and social perspectives Artificial intelligence, beyond being a technological innovation in education, is a powerful phenomenon that fundamentally transforms how children perceive and experience the world. This transformation holds particular significance for gifted students who demonstrate cognitive flexibility and high learning potential. The purpose of this study is to examine, in a multidimensional manner, gifted primary school students’ perceptions of artificial intelligence in terms of cognitive, emotional, social, safety-ethical dimensions, as well as its future roles and uses. The study was conducted using a qualitative research design. The participants consisted of a total of 17 primary school students (nine girls and eight boys) enrolled in a Science and Art Center in Türkiye, selected through criterion sampling. Data were collected using a semi-structured interview form consisting of 21 questions prepared across different dimensions related to artificial intelligence and were analyzed through content analysis. title: Theory-practice gap in a resource-dependent field: Physical education teachers' attitudes towards educational research
text_snippet: Theory-practice gap in a resource-dependent field: Physical education teachers' attitudes towards educational research Physical education is a resource-dependent field, and the gap between educational research and classroom practice can be evident here. This study examines the attitudes of physical education teachers working in a rural/resource-constrained context towards educational research, using a convergent parallel mixed-methods design. Quantitative data were collected from 166 physical education teachers using the Teacher Attitude Scale Towards Educational Research; qualitative data were supported by four open-ended questions. The findings reveal that while teachers acknowledge theoretical value of research, they are skeptical about its applicability. Qualitative analyses indicate that this dilemma stems from structural barriers such as lack of facilities/equipment, time constraints, and a perceived lack of practical utility in research outputs. While no significant differences were observed in demographic variables (age, seniority, school level, school type), a marginally significant trend favoring female teachers was detected. title: A meta-analysis of the rights of the children in primary school
text_snippet: A meta-analysis of the rights of the children in primary school Children’s rights education is not limited to conveying rights at a conceptual level; it is a holistic process that aims for children to internalize these rights by experiencing them in daily life. This educational approach fosters students’ awareness and attitudes toward rights, while also promoting the adoption of democratic values such as justice, equality, and participation at an early age. Although child rights education has been extensively studied, research in Türkiye has been largely descriptive, and empirical evidence is limited. Furthermore, no previous meta-analysis has synthesized findings within the context of Turkish primary schools. A rights-based learning environment supports children’s social and emotional development, enabling both individual empowerment and active citizenship in social life. This study aims to determine the effects of children’s rights education programs implemented at the primary school level on students’ levels of knowledge, attitudes, and awareness. title: Academic procrastination in focus: Understanding the roles of academic self-efficacy and academic buoyancy among English-majors
text_snippet: Academic procrastination in focus: Understanding the roles of academic self-efficacy and academic buoyancy among English-majors Despite knowing the importance of timely academic engagement, many students continue to delay their academic responsibilities, raising questions about the psychological factors that influence academic procrastination. Thus, this study focuses on academic procrastination and explores how academic self-efficacy and academic buoyancy may contribute to its mitigation, with a specific focus on the potentially mediating role of academic buoyancy on the relationship between academic self-efficacy and academic procrastination. The study involved 170 undergraduate students majoring in English at a state university in Türkiye. Quantitative in nature, this study utilized structural equation modelling technique to investigate the interplay among academic self-efficacy, academic buoyancy and academic procrastination. The correlational analyses found statistically significant relationships among all variables, viz. positive correlation between academic self-efficacy and academic buoyancy, and negative correlation between academic procrastination and academic self-efficacy / academic buoyancy. title: Investigation of pre-service teachers’ information security knowledge and information security awareness through canonical correlation analysis
text_snippet: Investigation of pre-service teachers’ information security knowledge and information security awareness through canonical correlation analysis The purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between pre-service teachers' information security knowledge and information security awareness. In this context, a correlational research design, one of the general survey models, was used in the study. The sample consisted of a total of 284 pre-service teachers, 112 from the Department of Elementary Mathematics Education and 172 from the Department of Early Childhood Education. In the study, data were collected using the Information Security Knowledge Scale and the Information Security Awareness Scale. Descriptive statistics and canonical correlation analysis were used to analyze the data. The results indicated that pre-service teachers' information security awareness levels were high across the total scale and sub-dimensions. In contrast, their information security knowledge levels were moderate across the total scale and sub-dimensions. In addition, a significant positive relationship was found between pre-service teachers' information security knowledge and awareness. title: Language learning anxiety among learners of Turkish as a foreign language: A mixed methods study
text_snippet: Language learning anxiety among learners of Turkish as a foreign language: A mixed methods study This study aims to reveal the Turkish language learning anxieties of international learners studying Turkish as a foreign language and the underlying reasons for these anxieties, using a mixed research approach. In this context, a mixed-methods explanatory sequential design was adopted. The study was conducted with 167 international students at B1, B2, and C1 levels at two state universities in the 2024 academic year. In the study, quantitative data were collected using the Scale of Anxiety in Learning Turkish for Foreigners. The data were analyzed using the independent samples t-test to examine differences in anxiety scores by gender, and one-way ANOVA to examine differences by native language, number of known foreign languages, and language level. To support and elaborate on the quantitative data, interviews were conducted with 37 international students at the end of the study, providing qualitative data. title: Turkish adaptation of the Real Relationship Inventory–Therapist Form: A validity and reliability study
text_snippet: Turkish adaptation of the Real Relationship Inventory–Therapist Form: A validity and reliability study This study aimed to adapt the Real Relationship Inventory–Therapist Form (RRI-T) into Turkish and to examine its psychometric properties. The real relationship is widely regarded as the most fundamental component of the therapeutic relationship, yet no Turkish instrument previously existed to assess it. The study group consisted of 420 mental health professionals working across Türkiye. The scale was adapted following the recommended cross-cultural adaptation steps, including translation, back-translation, expert committee review, and a pilot application. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted to examine construct validity. title: Türkiye Century Education Model 2024 middle school mathematics teaching program differentiation through support: Program and teacher perspectives
text_snippet: Türkiye Century Education Model 2024 middle school mathematics teaching program differentiation through support: Program and teacher perspectives This study aims to examine the “differentiation through support” component included in the Türkiye Century Education Model 2024 Middle School Mathematics Curriculum and to explore teachers’ views on the concept of differentiation. The research was conducted in two stages. In the first stage, the support practices within the curriculum document were evaluated using the document analysis method, during which categories and codes were developed. In the second stage, semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten mathematics teachers to investigate their knowledge, experiences, and awareness regarding differentiation within the curriculum. The study was designed as a qualitative study, and the interview data were analyzed using content analysis. The findings indicate that the curriculum’s support approach is predominantly based on process differentiation, with the most common differentiation practices focusing on concept formation, materials use, and modeling strategies. title: The use of background music in educational settings
text_snippet: The use of background music in educational settings This study is a theoretical review that examines, from a holistic perspective, the effects of background music used in classroom settings on students’ cognitive, affective, and social learning processes. Drawing on contemporary research in educational psychology, environmental structuring, learning theories, and special education, the contributions of background music to learning efficiency have been analyzed multidimensionally. The literature indicates that appropriately selected background music can increase attention span, support performance in cognitive tasks, and positively influence classroom interactions by facilitating students’ emotional regulation. In particular, instrumental and low-tempo genres such as lo-fi, classical, and ambient music have been reported to yield beneficial outcomes for both general student populations and individuals with special educational needs, including ADHD, autism, and learning disabilities. However, the effects of music emerge through complex interactions among multiple variables, including individual differences, task type, musical preference, and classroom atmosphere. On a theoretical level, the study is framed within Cognitive Load Theory

title: Descriptive analysis of findings related to the family experiences of individuals with autism
text_snippet: Descriptive analysis of findings related to the family experiences of individuals with autism This study aims to identify the issues faced by families of children with autism spectrum disorder in education and daily life, and to suggest ways to address these issues. The research findings were analyzed using descriptive content analysis, focusing on qualitative research conducted with children with ASD and their families. Within this scope, 21 postgraduate theses identified from the National Thesis Centre of the Council of Higher Education that met the specified criteria were included in the analysis. The theses were examined in terms of descriptive data, including the research method, design, data collection tool, type of analysis, characteristics of the participants, the university, and the year. Then, the results obtained were analyzed thematically. The analysis identified five main themes: 'Family participation', 'challenges of autism', 'initial recognition of ASD', 'support process', and 'parents' positive views'. The findings revealed that families attempted to participate in the educational process but encountered limitations regarding cooperation and support services. title: Family participation in emergency distance learning: A multiple case study on sixth-grade students, parents, and teachers
text_snippet: Family participation in emergency distance learning: A multiple case study on sixth-grade students, parents, and teachers This study aims to examine the views of sixth-grade students, parents, and teachers regarding family participation in the distance learning process. A multiple case study, one of the qualitative research methods, forms the basic design of the study. The study group consists of five mathematics teachers, ten students, and the parents of these students, selected using maximum diversity sampling. The data for the study were obtained through interviews. An ethical committee approval was obtained prior to the research. The data obtained were analyzed using in-depth content analysis. The findings showed that family participation was considered important by all participants, but participants' knowledge about implementing family participation in distance education was not sufficient. It was also found that the activities students carried out with their families contributed to their happiness, the development of their cognitive and affective skills, and had a positive impact on their attitudes towards mathematics lessons. title: Teaching clerical skills to individuals with autism in a skill-specific workplace with video modeling
text_snippet: Teaching clerical skills to individuals with autism in a skill-specific workplace with video modeling Teaching vocational skills to individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is crucial for their independent living and quality of life. This research aims to teach vocational skills to individuals with ASD using video modeling. In addition, the study investigated the maintenance and generalization of the acquired skills. Furthermore, the study examined the views of individuals with ASD and their parents regarding the research. Finally, the participants' levels of non-targeted information acquisition were examined. Using a multiple-probe model between participants, one of the single-case research designs, we used the video modeling method to teach three male participants aged 15 to 19 with ASD the skills of document sorting, document carrying, and photocopying. We assessed skill generalization at 1, 5, and 12 weeks. We also examined whether participants acquired non-targeted information related to each target skill. title: A meta-synthesis study on research related to sustainable development in social studies education
text_snippet: A meta-synthesis study on research related to sustainable development in social studies education This study aims to examine research on sustainable development in the context of social studies education through a meta-synthesis approach. A total of 22 studies (19 articles and three theses) conducted between 2009 and 2023 were systematically analyzed. The data were examined using document analysis and descriptive techniques, and coded and interpreted in MAXQDA 24. The findings reveal that the way sustainable development is addressed within social studies education still contains several conceptual and pedagogical limitations. Most studies lack sufficient transparency in sampling processes and analysis procedures. Research has predominantly focused on curriculum review, textbook analysis, and pre-service teacher awareness, demonstrating that sustainable development is often handled superficially in instructional materials and curricular objectives. Despite this, the social studies course has been shown to play a significant role in enhancing students' awareness and understanding of sustainability issues. title: Preschool teachers’ views on philosophy education and philosophical inquiry
text_snippet: Preschool teachers’ views on philosophy education and philosophical inquiry This study which using a descriptive qualitative research model aims to reveal the experiences, perceptions, and practices of preschool teachers regarding philosophy education and philosophical inquiry methodsA total of 20 female preschool teachers from different schools participated in the study. Data were collected using semi-structured interview forms and analyzed through thematic analysis. The research findings indicate that teachers define philosophy education as a process that teaches thinking, facilitates knowledge-oriented questioning, provides different perspectives, is comprehensive, and is grounded in theoretical knowledge and professional practice. The philosophical inquiry method, on the other hand, is regarded as a process that promotes deep questioning, requires practice and training, fosters the development and grounding of ideas, and can be used in daily life without formal education. The study emphasizes that while philosophy education and philosophical inquiry are distinct processes, they are interconnected, and philosophical inquiry is a fundamental component of philosophy education. title: The effect of psychological flexibility and intolerance of uncertainty on decision-making styles in university students
text_snippet: The effect of psychological flexibility and intolerance of uncertainty on decision-making styles in university students The purpose of this study is to examine the effects of psychological flexibility and intolerance of uncertainty on individuals' decision-making styles among university students. The study was designed as a correlational survey model, and data were collected from 381 university students aged 18-29. Participants completed the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale, the Psychological Flexibility Scale, and the Rational and Intuitive Decision Making Styles Scale. Multiple linear regression analysis was used in the data analysis. The dependent variables of this study are the subdimensions of decision-making styles, namely rational decision making and intuitive decision making. The independent variables are the subdimensions of psychological flexibility, which include acceptance, being present, defusion, self as context, values, and committed action. The other independent variable are the subdimensions of intolerance of uncertainty, specifically future-oriented anxiety and inhibitory anxiety. text_snippet: The effect of the individualised instruction model on students' attitudes towards physical education and sport: Experimental study The aim of this study is to examine the effect of the individualised teaching model on students' attitudes towards physical education and sports. At the beginning of the study, after matching the groups, 30 students (15 in the experimental group and 15 in the control group) in the 9th grade formed the study group through random assignment. title: Social studies teachers' perspectives on water literacy
text_snippet: Social studies teachers' perspectives on water literacy Water is considered the fundamental source of life and is among the most important issues requiring collective effort from all segments of society for its protection. Water resources are under significant threat due to factors such as the continuously growing human population, air pollution, and unconscious consumption of resources. This situation highlights the importance of the concept of water literacy regarding water, which is recognized as the most indispensable source of life in a changing and developing world. Teachers bear the most important responsibility in fostering this concept. The purpose of this study is to determine social studies teachers' views on water literacy. The research was conducted using a "phenomenological" design. The study group consists of 20 social studies teachers working in Diyarbakır during the spring semester of the 2022-2023 academic year. title: Strengthening social-emotional skills in female individuals: Implementation and evaluation of an intervention program
text_snippet: Strengthening social-emotional skills in female individuals: Implementation and evaluation of an intervention program This research aims to examine the effectiveness of an eight-week intervention program designed to develop social-emotional skills in adolescents. The study used a quasi-experimental design with a pre-test–post-test control group. The study group consisted of 24 female students (experimental=12, control=12) aged 14–16. The Social-Emotional Skills Psychoeducation Program, prepared by the Ministry of National Education, was administered to the experimental group, while no specific intervention was provided to the control group. The EPOCH Well-Being Scale, adapted for adolescents, was used as the data collection tool. The data were analyzed using independent-samples t-tests, paired-samples t-tests, and a mixed-design ANOVA in SPSS 27. The findings indicated a significant increase in the experimental group from pre-test to post-test, whereas no significant change was observed in the control group. Consequently, the social-emotional skills program was found to be effective in increasing adolescents' well-being. title: Interdisciplinary Teaching Design Self-Efficacy Scale: The validity and reliability study
text_snippet: Interdisciplinary Teaching Design Self-Efficacy Scale: The validity and reliability study The aim of this study is to develop a valid and reliable instrument to assess teachers’ self-efficacy in designing interdisciplinary teaching. During the scale development process, the scaling by cumulative sums approach based on participant responses was employed. Validity evidence was gathered through content and construct validity procedures. An item pool was generated based on focus group interviews and a comprehensive literature review, followed by expert review for content validation. The study sample comprised 350 teachers for exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and 231 teachers for confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). The final version of the scale obtained through analyses consists of 21 items measured on an 11-point scale ranging from 0 to 100, structured under two factors, namely, Competencies and Challenges. The scale demonstrated high reliability, with Cronbach's alpha coefficients of 0.95 and 0.92 for the respective factors. The total variance explained by the two subscales collectively is 66.21%.
